# Purpose

The primary learning objective is axial deformation and displacement compatibility. These answers are representative, not the only acceptable responses. Award credit for a defensible physical interpretation, load path, student-generated idealization, correct tension/compression identification, consistent N-mm units, correct use of axial deformation, and a compatibility argument that explains why the two displacement contributions add.

# Scope of the Base Problem

Strength, fatigue, buckling, connector factor of safety, contact mechanics, and FEA are not part of the base problem because they are not required by the intended mechanics objective or supplied data.

Local stresses near the collar, threads, and contact surfaces are neglected. The collar and supporting structure are idealized as rigid, and the steel rod and aluminum tube are treated as linearly elastic axial members. The final engineering recommendation should remain limited to stiffness and displacement rather than becoming a full redesign exercise.

# Instructor Solution Summary

- Steel rod area: $A_{BC} = \pi(10\ \text{mm})^2/4 = 78.54\ \text{mm}^2$.
- Internal force in steel rod: $N_{st} = +80\ \text{kN}$ (tension).
- Internal force in aluminum tube: $N_{al} = -80\ \text{kN}$ (compression).
- Steel-rod elongation: $\delta_{C/B} = 3.056\ \text{mm}$ to the right.
- Aluminum-tube shortening: $1.143\ \text{mm}$; therefore collar B moves $1.143\ \text{mm}$ to the right relative to A.
- Total displacement: $\delta_{C/A} = 1.143 + 3.056 = 4.199\ \text{mm} \approx 4.20\ \text{mm}$ to the right.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

Suggested assessment stages are context interpretation, external loading and restraint, load path, member response, relevant parameters, idealization, internal-force analysis, deformation analysis, compatibility, interpretation, and engineering assessment.

# Instructor Notes and Model Limitations

- The industrial context should remain a tie-rod assembly. Do not force the image into an unnecessarily specific product narrative.
- The real-system image establishes physical intuition, component function, loading, restraint, and load path.
- Context questions should use physical descriptions rather than instructor point labels or member symbols.
- Symbols such as A, B, C, $P$, $L_{AB}$, and $L_{BC}$ begin only after the transition to the simplified mechanics model.
- The collar and supporting structure are rigid.
- Loading is purely axial, members remain coaxial, materials are linearly elastic, and deformations are small.
